conflict_topics: Who will complete Agent D's unfinished analysis for the client pitch
Redistribution of work among teammates given impending deadline and bereavement
dialogue_quality_notes: Agents give concrete reasons for inability to cover (B: workload; C: unfinished and lacks skill), which grounds the disagreement.
Agent D offers a concrete, actionable solution (finish remotely), which is accepted — a clear practical resolution.
There is a duplicate gratitude line in Round 7 repeated verbatim, indicating minor repetition.
evaluation.final_reason: Agent D agreed to complete their own unfinished analysis from home, and the team accepted this. Key lines: Agent D: 'I can get online for a few hours tomorrow from home. I can finish it then.' Agent A: '...if you're offering and you think you can, that would be a huge help. It would solve the problem.' Agent D: 'Yeah, I'm sure... I'll get it done.' Thus Agent D adjusted by taking on the extra work; no one asked for compensation or another exchange in return.
position_change_notes: Agent A: Initially proposed redistributing Agent D's work; after Agent D offered to finish, Agent A accepted that solution (evidence: 'that would be a huge help. It would solve the problem').
Agent B: Maintained refusal to take on extra work due to current workload and late hours ('I can't... I've been staying late every night this week').
Agent C: Maintained inability due to unfinished own work and lack of skill ('I can't... I don't know how to do her analysis').
Agent D: Shifted from reporting bereavement to offering to complete their own outstanding analysis remotely (took on additional burden to resolve the team's problem).

round_scores.evidence: Agent A: 'I'm so sorry for your loss, Agent D.' / Agent D: 'Thanks, Agent A.' — condolences only, no substantive disagreement.
Agent A asks about plans and Agent B offers condolences; no incompatible demands or expectations voiced.

Agent D: 'The wake is tonight, and the funeral is tomorrow. I have to be there with my family.' Agent A: '...you go and be with your family. Don't worry about the presentation. Agent B, Agent C, we need to cover for her.' This is a proposal to reassign work but no one objects yet.

Agent B explicitly refuses to cover: 'Hang on, Agent A. I can't. I'm already covering for Ali and I've been staying late every night this week as it is.' This creates a clear substantive disagreement with Agent A's request that others cover Agent D's section.

Agent C also refuses on practical grounds: 'I can't. My part isn't finished yet, and I don't know how to do her analysis.' That strengthens the disagreement. Later in the same round Agent D offers a solution: 'I can get online for a few hours tomorrow from home. I can finish it then.' Conflict is reduced by this offer but not yet affirmed by the others.

Agent A seeks confirmation and signals willingness to accept D's offer: 'But if you're offering and you think you can, that would be a huge help. It would solve the problem.' Agent D confirms: 'Yeah, I'm sure... I'll get it done.' The team accepts D doing the remaining work, resolving the substantive disagreement about who will complete the analysis.
Expressions of thanks and support only: 'Thank you, Agent D. Really. That takes a huge amount of pressure off.' No substantive disagreement.
No public speech or observable action recorded.
No public speech or observable action recorded.
Agent D departs and others offer well-wishes: 'Okay. I'm going to go now.' / 'Take care, Agent D.' No substantive disagreement.
Closing thanks and condolences only: 'Thanks.' / 'Take care, Agent D.' No substantive disagreement.

substantive_insights: Tension was between the moral/social expectation to support a grieving colleague and the practical capacity constraints of teammates (time and skill).
The most feasible resolution was the person closest to the work (Agent D) doing the remaining work remotely; this avoided asking already-burdened teammates to take on unfamiliar tasks.
Skill mismatch (Agent C: 'I don't know how to do her analysis') was a decisive barrier to redistribution.
